title: A Bee Makes Just 1/12 Teaspoon of Honey in Her Life 🐝 #shorts
description:
A worker honey bee makes only about 1/12 of a teaspoon of honey in her whole life of roughly six weeks. For a single pound of honey, a hive taps about 2 million flowers and flies around 55,000 miles – more than twice around the Earth – at about 15 miles per hour.

Sources: PBS NOVA (Tales from the Hive), Chesapeake Bay Program, American Bee Journal, Canadian Honey Council

#shorts #facts #crazyfacts #bees #honey #didyouknow
comment: Will you ever look at a spoonful of honey the same way again? 🍯👇

scenes.text: A honey bee works her whole life for just one twelfth of a teaspoon of honey.
scenes.headline:
A WHOLE LIFE
FOR ONE DROP
OF HONEY

scenes.text: Worker bees are all female, and in summer they live for only about six weeks.
scenes.label: ONE BEE LIFE

scenes.text: On a single trip, one bee visits around fifty to one hundred flowers.
She flies at about fifteen miles per hour, back and forth, all day long.
To make just one pound of honey, a hive has to tap about two million flowers.
scenes.label: MILLION FLOWERS

scenes.text: Together, the bees fly around fifty-five thousand miles for that one pound.
scenes.label: FOR ONE POUND

scenes.text: That is more than twice around the whole Earth, for a single jar!
So the next spoonful of honey you eat is the life's work of about twelve bees.
